items.text: Deceased artists are performing as holograms, and they are even releasing music through digital updates; however, this technology raises many concerns. The concerns started with the holographic resurrection of Tupac Shakur at the 2012 Coachella Music Festival, which critics called creepy. The use of the technology continued with tours for jazz rock musician Frank Zappa, opera singer Maria Callas, and R&B singer Amy Winehouse. The family of pop singer Selena Quintanilla announced a new posthumous album, and it’ll digitally age the artist’s voice to make it sound as if she were still alive. Over the past years, many have questioned whether these posthumous performances are celebrating a legacy or exploiting the dead. A documentary about food icon Anthony Bourdain used AI to recreate his voice and say things that he never said. This incident raised concerns about what happens to our digital likeness without our permission. Difficult words: resurrection (return from the dead), posthumous (happening after a person’s death), legacy (something that’s left when a person dies). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Modern technologies make it possible for dead singers to return to the stage. Their holograms can sing old hits as well as new songs, but not all people like the technology. Tupac Shakur was the first person to perform after his death at the Coachella Music Festival in 2012. Since that time, people saw many dead artists perform. Examples are Frank Zappa or Amy Winehouse. Some people didn’t like the performances, and they called them creepy . People asked if such performances celebrated the artists or if they were clever ways to make money. Pop star Selena Quintanilla died in 1995, but since that time, her family released 24 albums by her. On the last album, her voice was digitally changed to sound older. In a documentary about the celebrity chef Anthony Bourdain, filmmakers used modern technologies so he said things which he never really said. Difficult words: hologram (a digital image of something, which looks like a real thing), creepy (unpleasant or scary), release (to make something available to the public). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Modern technologies can make dead singers sing again. Their holograms can sing old hits and new songs, too. The first performance of a hologram happens in 2012. People can see Tupac Shakur at a music festival. Tupac dies in 1996. Some people don’t like his hologram. They say that it is scary. Other artists sing after they die. They are, for example, Frank Zappa or Amy Winehouse. Some people think that the technology makes the artists seem alive . Other people think that this is only a way to make money. Pop star Selena Quintanilla dies in 1995. Her family makes 24 albums with her songs since 1995. Her voice is different on the newest album. Modern technologies make her sound older. Difficult words: hologram (a digital image of someone or something), performance (when you play or sing at a show, concert, or other event), alive (not dead). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In New Zealand, the Verheul family was hiking in the Kepler Track, a 60-kilometer hiking trail. They reached a hut to rest and camp, and they put their GoPro camera outside to film kea parrots when a kleptomaniac kea stole the camera. The bird escaped while the airborne GoPro recorded the flight, and then it recorded the bird attacking it and stripping off pieces of plastic. The family followed the sounds, and the kea flew away when they approached. The son recovered the GoPro as it continued to record. The kea is famous for being curious and mischievous . The parrot steals things from people to investigate them, such as wallets, jewelry, lunches, and windshield wipers. Difficult words: kleptomaniac (a person or animal that steals many things), strip off (to pull off in long strips), mischievous (playfully making trouble). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In New Zealand, a family was hiking along a 60-kilometer hiking trail. They stopped to rest and camp; they put their GoPro outside to record kea parrots when a kleptomaniac kea stole the camera. The bird escaped while the GoPro recorded its flight, and then the camera recorded the bird attacking it and removing pieces of plastic. The kea flew away when the family found it. The camera was still recording. The kea is famous for being curious and playfully making trouble. The parrot steals things from people to learn about them, such as wallets, jewelry, lunches, and windshield wipers. Difficult words: kleptomaniac (a person or animal that steals many things), GoPro (a camera that records while you are doing activities), curious (when you want to learn). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In New Zealand, a family is hiking on a long trail. They stop at a camp. Parrots fly around them. They put their camera outside. They record the parrots. One parrot steals the camera. The camera records the bird flying. Then it records the bird biting it. The bird takes some of it apart. The bird flies away when the family finds the camera. The camera is still recording. This parrot is famous. It likes to steal things. It likes to learn about things. Sometimes it steals wallets, jewelry, lunches, and car parts. Difficult words: parrot (a colorful bird), record (to film or make a video), steal (to take someone’s thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ethiopia has lifted a ban on Bitcoin mining, using surplus electricity from its new Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, the largest in Africa. Mining is an energy-intensive process, but the country currently produces more power than its grid can distribute. Until more households are connected, Bitcoin companies are allowed to use this extra energy. Fees from miners, around 220 million dollars in the last year, are intended to help expand the national grid. The government still aims for universal access to electricity by 2030, though this target looks difficult to achieve. Mining in Ethiopia is very profitable . Producing one Bitcoin costs about 20,000 dollars, mainly due to electricity, while it sells for more than 100,000. Cheap energy makes Ethiopia attractive compared to countries like those in the EU, where costs are much higher. Experts say this is only a temporary measure until domestic demand grows. As Bitcoin gains wider acceptance globally, Ethiopia could become an important hub for crypto mining. Difficult words: surplus (an extra amount), profitable (generating profit), hub (the main center or important place where many activities happen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ethiopia now lets companies mine Bitcoin again. The country built a big dam, which makes a lot of electricity. But many people are still not connected to the power grid . So the government sells the extra energy to Bitcoin miners. These companies pay big fees, which help build more power lines. Last year, they paid about 220 million dollars. The plan is to give electricity to everyone by 2030, but this is hard to achieve. Mining Bitcoin in Ethiopia is cheap. It costs about 20,000 dollars, but one Bitcoin sells for more than 100,000. Therefore, Ethiopia is attractive for miners. In Europe, electricity is much more expensive. For now, Bitcoin is growing, and experts believe Ethiopia can become an important place for mining. Difficult words: power grid (wires, cables, and stations which carry electricity from power plants to homes and businesses), attractive (something that makes people interested). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ethiopia makes a lot of electricity with a new big dam . But many people in the country still have no power in their homes. The government gives extra energy to Bitcoin companies. These companies pay money, and the money helps build more power lines. The goal is to bring electricity to every home one day. Mining Bitcoin in Ethiopia is cheap. One Bitcoin costs about 20,000 dollars to make. But people can sell it for more than 100,000 dollars. That is why many companies want to mine in Ethiopia. Experts say that this is not forever. Later, more people in Ethiopia will use the electricity. But now Bitcoin is strong, and Ethiopia can grow as a place for mining. Difficult words: dam (a big wall across a river), goal (what you want to do or reach in the future), mine (to get minerals and other things from the ground; to make new coins with computers). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new OECD report shows where young Europeans have the highest university education. Ireland leads with two-thirds of adults aged 25 to 34 holding a degree in 2024. Luxembourg follows with 65% and Lithuania with 58%. At the bottom are Czechia with 33% and Hungary and Italy with 32%. The report highlights major contrasts across the EU in terms of higher education access. Family background plays a key role. In every country, young people whose parents studied at university are much more likely to obtain a degree themselves. Denmark shows the smallest gap: 70% of young adults with graduate parents have a degree, compared with 49% of those whose parents did not. Poland has the largest gap, with 79% versus only 11%. The OECD also stresses the benefits of higher education. A degree is linked to better chances of employment, higher salaries, and improved health. Education is not only about knowledge but also about the quality of life. Difficult words: contrast (a clear difference), obtain (to get something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new report shows that young adults in Europe study at very different levels. In Ireland, two out of three people aged 25–34 have a degree , the highest in the EU. Luxembourg has 65% and Lithuania has 58%. At the bottom are Czechia with 33% and Hungary and Italy with 32%. The report also explains that family background matters a lot. In Denmark, 70% of young people with university parents have a degree, compared to 49% of those with non-university parents. In Poland, the difference is bigger, 79% compared to only 11%. Education gives people many advantages . People with higher education can find jobs more easily, earn more money, and live healthier lives. Difficult words: degree (a certificate from university), background (family or social situation), advantage (something helpful or useful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new report shows how many young people in Europe finish university. Ireland is number one: two out of three young adults aged 25–34 have a degree . Luxembourg has 65% and Lithuania has 58%. Czechia is low with 33%. Hungary and Italy are the lowest with 32%. Family makes a big difference . In Denmark, 70% of young people with university parents have a degree. Only 49% of young people without such parents have one. In Poland, the gap is bigger: 79% versus 11%. Studying more helps people in life. With higher education , people can get better jobs and more money, and stay healthier. Difficult words: degree (a certificate from a university), difference (when something is not the same), education (learning in schools). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brazil’s former president Jair Bolsonaro has been sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a military coup after losing the 2022 election. Supreme Court justices ruled that Bolsonaro, a former army officer, tried to destroy democracy by getting back to power. Judge Alexandre de Moraes said Bolsonaro led a criminal organisation that sought to return Brazil to dictatorship between 2021 and January 2023, when his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasília. Four of five judges voted to convict him, while one argued there was insufficient proof. Several of Bolsonaro’s allies, including ex-defense ministers and close aides , were also convicted. The verdict sparked celebrations among Bolsonaro’s opponents, who see it as justice for years of attacks on democracy, the environment, and minorities. But supporters denounced the trial as political. US officials, including Donald Trump, criticized the ruling, while Brazil’s government rejected foreign pressure. Experts warn that Bolsonaro’s political movement remains alive, and his allies may still try to overturn the conviction or push for amnesty in the future. Difficult words: dictatorship (a kind of government where one person has all the power), insufficient (not enough), aide (a person who helps or works closely with someone important), amnesty (official forgiveness for crimes). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A top court sent Brazil’s ex-president Jair Bolsonaro to 27 years in prison. Judges said he tried to plan a military coup after losing the 2022 election. Four of the five judges voted that he was guilty . They said Bolsonaro wanted to end democracy and bring back dictatorship . His supporters attacked government buildings in January 2023, and several of his supporters also went to court. Only one judge said that there was not enough information to show that Bolsonaro did something wrong. Many Brazilians celebrated, but Bolsonaro’s supporters said the trial was unfair. Some US politicians, including Donald Trump, also criticized the court. Experts say Bolsonaro’s political movement is still strong, and some people may try to win power again or ask for amnesty . Difficult words: military coup (when soldiers take power by force), guilty (when the court says that you did a crime), dictatorship (a kind of government where one person has all the power), amnesty (when the government forgives a group of people for breaking the law). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Brazil, ex-president Jair Bolsonaro will go to prison for 27 years. Judges say that Bolsonaro wants to stay in power after losing the 2022 election . The judges say that Bolsonaro wants to end democracy. In January 2023, his supporters break into government buildings. Four judges say that this is true; only one judge says that there is not enough information about it. Some of Bolsonaro’s friends go to prison, too. Many people in Brazil are happy. But others are angry. The day that it is unfair. Some US leaders, like Donald Trump, also support Bolsonaro. Experts say that Bolsonaro’s group is still strong and may try to bring him back. Difficult words: in power (when you are the leader of a country or organization), election (when people choose a leader), supporter (a person who likes or helps a person or group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Greece is facing a severe demographic crisis. Births in 2022 dropped below 77,000, the lowest in nearly a century, while deaths reached 140,000. As a result, the population is shrinking rapidly and could fall by 25% by 2070, much higher than the European average. The fertility rate is now just 1.35 children per woman, and women are having their first child at an average age of 32. This decline has forced the closure of more than 750 schools, over 5% of the total, due to a lack of students. The Ministry of Education reports that primary school enrollment has fallen by 19% in the past seven years. Greece created its first Ministry for Demographic Policy in 2023, but solutions remain difficult. Governments worldwide face similar problems, from Japan and South Korea to much of Europe and the Americas. Low fertility leads to aging societies, labor shortages, and slower economic growth. Experts say the root causes are high living costs, expensive housing, and poor childcare options. Without deep reforms, the crisis will worsen. Difficult words: fertility rate (an average number of children per woman), enrollment (the number of students registered in schools). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Greece is in trouble because people are not having enough babies. In 2022, fewer than 77,000 babies were born, while 140,000 people died. Experts say the population could shrink by 25% by 2070. Women now have their first child at age 32, and the fertility rate is only 1.35, one of the lowest in Europe. Because there are fewer children, more than 750 schools, about 5%, are closing. In the last seven years, the number of primary students has dropped by 19%. This is not only a Greek problem. Japan, South Korea, and many other countries also face falling birth rates . The main reasons are high costs of living, missing childcare, and expensive housing. Experts say that without better support, people will keep having children later and later. Difficult words: fertility rate (an average number of children per woman), primary student (a child who is 4 to 10 years old), birth rate (the number of children born per thousand of population in one year). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Greece has a big problem. People are not having many babies. In 2022, only 77,000 babies are born, but 140,000 people die. This means the population is getting smaller. Greek women usually have their first baby at age 32. The number of children per woman is only 1.35. Because there are fewer kids, Greece will close more than 750 schools. Schools lose 100,000 students over the last seven years. Other countries also have this problem, like Japan and South Korea. But many European countries have this problem too. Experts say that life costs too much for young people, especially houses, childcare, and education . People wait longer to marry and have children. Experts say that governments must help, or the problem will get worse. Difficult words: population (all the people in a country), especially (mainly), education (schools). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has inaugurated the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, calling it a historic achievement. Built over 14 years on the Blue Nile, it is Africa’s largest hydroelectric project, with the capacity to produce more than 5,000 megawatts of power. The dam is expected to supply electricity to millions of Ethiopians and even export power to neighboring countries. For many families who still live without electricity, this project represents hope for a better future. Ordinary citizens contributed to its cost through donations and government bonds, making it a symbol of national unity after years of conflict. However, the dam is controversial . Egypt and Sudan worry it will reduce their water supply from the Nile, particularly during droughts . Negotiations among the three countries have failed to produce a binding agreement, and diplomatic tensions remain high. Ethiopia insists the dam won’t harm downstream nations. Beyond electrification , the project is central to Ethiopia’s goal of becoming a regional economic power. Difficult words: inaugurate (to officially open or begin something important), controversial (causing public disagreement), drought (a long period without rain), electrification (the process of bringing electricity to places). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ethiopia opened the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, the biggest in Africa. It stands on the Blue Nile, and it took 14 years to build. The dam can produce huge amounts of electricity, enough for millions of people in Ethiopia and nearby countries. Many families without power hope their lives will improve. People across Ethiopia gave money through donations and bonds , and many see the dam as a nationa l project. But Egypt and Sudan are worried. They say the dam could cut their water from the Nile, especially in dry times. Talks between the three countries didn’t bring an agreement, so the tension continues. Ethiopia says the dam will not harm others and believes it will help the country grow stronger. Difficult words: donation (money which people give to help a person or organization), bond (an official paper which people buy to support a project), national (related to all the people of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ethiopia has a new dam on the Blue Nile. It is the biggest dam in Africa. It takes 14 years to build it. The dam can make electricity for millions of people. Many homes in Ethiopia have no power, so people believe that the dam will change this. Some families give money to help build it. The government says that it is a project for the whole country. But not everyone is happy. Egypt and Sudan worry that the dam will take away water from the Nile. They want to talk, but it is not easy to agree with each other. Ethiopia says that the dam is safe and will not hurt them. The dam will also give power to other countries. Many people see it as a great thing. Difficult words: dam (a big wall on a river which helps make electricity), project (a planned work or activity which takes a long time to do), agree (to have the same ideas or opinions as somebody else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poland says it has shot down several Russian drones that entered its airspace during an attack on Ukraine. The army described this as an act of aggression and a danger to Polish citizens. Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed the violation and said Poland was in close contact with NATO and its allies. Damaged drones and debris were found near the border, and airports, including Warsaw’s, were briefly closed. This event marks a dangerous escalation because it directly involves NATO territory. Analysts suggest it may be part of Russia’s hybrid warfare, which includes intimidation , espionage , and disinformation. NATO has responded calmly, but the timing raises concern since Russia is beginning large military exercises in Belarus. At the same time, European defense ministers are meeting in London to support Ukraine, while fighting in Donbas remains intense. Russia controls nearly all of Luhansk, but Ukraine still holds major cities in Donetsk. The future of the war remains uncertain. Difficult words: escalation (a situation becoming more serious and dangerous), intimidation (frightening or threatening someone), espionage (secretly collecting and reporting information). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Poland shot down Russian drones that flew into its airspace . The Polish army called this aggression a risk to people’s safety. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said many drones entered Poland, and those that were dangerous were destroyed. People found parts of the drones near the border, and airports, including Warsaw, closed for a short time. Tusk also said he is in contact with NATO and other allies . Experts say this may be part of Russia’s plan to test or scare NATO. At the same time, defense ministers from Poland and other countries are meeting in London to talk about more help for Ukraine. Fighting in Donbas continues, where Russia controls most of Luhansk, but Ukraine still holds some big cities in Donetsk. Difficult words: airspace (the air or sky above a country), aggression (a violent action), ally (a country that supports another one). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poland says it shoots down Russian drones. The drones fly into Poland during an attack on Ukraine. The Polish army says that this is dangerous for people. The prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that many drones come. He says NATO and other friends are helping Poland. Pieces of drones fall near the border. Some airports close, even Warsaw, but they open again later. Experts say that Russia wants to scare Poland and NATO. At the same time, leaders from Poland and Europe meet in London. They talk about helping Ukraine. In the east, Russia takes much land, but Ukraine still has some big cities. It is not the end of the war yet. Difficult words: airport (a place where planes land and take off), scare (to make someone feel worried or afraid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nepal is facing its worst political crisis in recent history. Massive protests broke out after the government banned social media platforms like Facebook and Instagram. Young people, frustrated with corruption, unemployment, and lack of opportunities, filled the streets. The government tried to stop them with a violent crackdown , killing 19 protesters and injuring many more. Instead of calming the situation, this violence made the public even angrier. They set fire to government buildings, including the Parliament and Supreme Court, and attacked ministers and opposition leaders. Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli eventually resigned, saying he wanted a political solution, but his departure has left Nepal in uncertainty. The army and president are calling for calm, but the future remains unclear. Many protesters demand younger leaders, and two names have appeared: Balendra Shah, the 35-year-old mayor of Kathmandu, and Rabi Lamichhane, a politician recently freed from prison. The coming days will decide whether the unrest ends or grows. Difficult words: crackdown (sudden strong action by police or army), unrest (a situation with protests and violence). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Nepal is going through a big crisis. The government banned many social media platforms, and thousands of young people took to the streets. People are angry about corruption , no jobs, and few chances for the future. The police and army tried to stop them with violence . Nineteen protesters died, and more were hurt. This made the protests even stronger. People burned government buildings and attacked both ministers and opposition leaders. Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli resigned after the chaos . He said he wanted peace, but people don’t know what will happen next. The president and the army ask everyone to stay calm. Some young leaders may take power, such as Balendra Shah or Rabi Lamichhane. The next days will be very important for Nepal. Difficult words: corruption (dishonest or illegal actions in government), violence (hurting somebody), chaos (a situation without order). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nepal has big problems now. The government stops Facebook, Instagram, and other social media. Young people feel angry because they have no jobs and no hope . Many people go into the streets. The army and police use guns and water to stop them. Nineteen people die, and many get hurt. The protests become bigger. People burn buildings like the Parliament and the Supreme Court. They also hit ministers and leaders. The prime minister, KP Sharma Oli, says that he cannot stay. He leaves his job. The president asks people to stay calm . Soldiers also ask people to stop fighting. But nobody knows what will happen. Some people want new young leaders. The next days are very important for Nepal. Difficult words: government (leaders of a country), hope (a feeling that something good will happen), calm (quiet and without worry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

From the 1990s until the early 2000s, hundreds of Roma women in Slovakia were forcibly sterilized without their consent , often immediately after childbirth. For the Roma culture, large families are a symbol of wealth and happiness, so this practice had devastating consequences. Many women lost the chance to have more children and suffered broken relationships, prejudice , and shame. Survivors like Veronica Duzdova and Zlatica Kalejova have shared their stories, describing how they only discovered the sterilization years later. Today, women and activists are fighting for justice. Their organization, based in Košice, offers support and legal help. Access to medical records has been a key obstacle, but new laws now allow evidence collection. Over 140 women in two regions alone were sterilized against their will. The Slovak government has apologized and is considering a bill to provide compensation, though public opinion remains divided. Survivors hope this painful chapter will finally close, recognizing their human rights and dignity . Difficult words: consent (permission to do something), prejudice (unfair negative opinion about people), dignity (feeling of respect for oneself). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Slovakia, doctors sterilized many Roma women in the 1990s and early 2000s, but the women didn’t know about it. This happened often right after birth. In Roma culture, having many children is very important, so these women lost something central to their lives. Some women discovered the truth years later, when they tried to have more children. Many also faced shame , sadness, and problems in their families. Victims and activists are now asking for compensation . Their group in Košice helps women collect medical records, which are proof of what happened. More than 140 women in two areas were affected. The Slovak government said sorry and may pay compensation, but the Slovak people have different opinions. Many Roma women still hope for fairness. Difficult words: central (very important), shame (a strong negative feeling in front of other people), compensation (money or help to make up for a loss or harm). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Slovakia, many Roma women have a big problem. In the 1990s, doctors sterilize them. It means that these women cannot have more children. The women do not agree. Some women only learn about it many years later, when they cannot have more babies. They feel sad. People judge them. In Roma culture, a big family is very important, so this hurts them a lot. Now, some women and helpers want fairness and money from the state. A group helps women and looks at hospital papers. More than 140 women in two places have this problem. The government says sorry and may give money, but not everyone in Slovakia agrees. The women still hope for fairness. Difficult words: sterilize (to make someone unable to have children), judge (to have an opinion about someone, often not a fair one), fairness (acting in a way which is right and fair). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists from the Chinese University of Hong Kong created a magnetic slime that squeezes through narrow spaces, encircles smaller objects, and heals itself. Magnets control the slime, and it can act as both a solid and a liquid. Scientists envisage that the slime could potentially be useful in the digestive system, such as in reducing the harm from accidentally swallowed objects like batteries. Scientists move the slime with external magnets. Although the magnetic parts are toxic, they’re safe when they’re covered in a silicone compound . The so-called soft robot can also bend, travel, and reshape to form O and C shapes. People on social media compared the dark blob to Flubber, the eponymous substance in the 1997 sci-fi film, and they described it as amazing and a bit terrifying. Difficult words: envisage (to imagine or expect something in the future), silicone compound (a colorless rubber-like substance), eponymous (named after something else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chinese scientists created a slime which can move. The slime has very small magnets, and scientists moved it with other magnets. The slime moved through very narrow spaces and formed a circle around other objects. It could bend and change its shape to make the O and C letters. The magnetic parts are toxic , but scientists covered them with silicone to make the slime safe. People on social media compared the slime to Flubber from the 1997 sci-fi movie. They said that it was amazing but a little scary, too. Scientists hope that it can be possible to use the slime in the digestive system . For example, it can help people when they swallow a small object, such as a battery. Difficult words: toxic (a very dangerous thing which can kill someone), silicone (a substance with no color, and which feels like rubber), digestive system (the body parts in the body, which take in food and drinks). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chinese scientists make a slime. The slime can move. The slime is full of very small magnets. They are dangerous for people. They are in a silicone substance . This makes them safe for people. Scientists use magnets to move the slime. The slime gets through very narrow spaces. It can make a circle. It can make the O and C shape. People on social media say that the slime looks like Flubber. Flubber is a substance from a 1997 sci-fi film. Scientists say that the slime could help people who swallow something dangerous, for example, a battery. Difficult words: silicone substance (a material which has no color, and it looks like rubber), narrow (little space between two things), swallow (to make food or drink go through the mouth and down to the stomach). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dubai resident and enthusiast Jimmy Grewal has an impressive collection of around 200 Apple computers and accessories. Grewal says that his collection is very important to him; it’s a snapshot into his childhood and his memories. He either owned or used all of the devices, or they were the ones that he wanted to own as a child. Many of the computers in Grewal’s collection weren’t commercially successful, and it was a sign for him that if you keep trying, eventually you would have success that the world would remember. Grewal will sell an Apple-1 computer on eBay to fund pop-up exhibitions of his collection. Last year, he was invited to an event where he met Steve Wozniak, one of the Apple founders, who signed an original Apple-1 computer for him. Difficult words: enthusiast (a person who’s very interested in a particular activity or subject), snapshot (a photograph that’s taken quickly; a picture of a memory), pop-up (temporary). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Jimmy Grewal lives in Dubai, and for all his life, Apple computers and devices have interested him. Grewal has a collection of about 200 Apple computers and accessories. Some of them are his own, and some of them are the ones which he wanted to have. Grewal said that the collection was special because when he looked at the old computers, he felt like looking at his own childhood . Grewal said that some of the computers weren’t very good, and not many people bought them. Yet for Grewal, they were a sign that if you work hard, you’ll be successful one day. He wants to sell some of his computers to make enough money to organize an exhibition . Difficult words: collection (a group of similar things that someone brings together), childhood (the time when someone is a child), exhibition (an event to display or share things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jimmy Grewal lives in Dubai. He loves Apple computers. He collects Apple computers and devices for all his life. Now he has more than 200 pieces. Some of the computers are his own. He also buys the computers which he does not have as a child. He says that looking at the computers is like looking at his childhood . Grewal wants to make an exhibition. An exhibition is an event to show things. He needs money for it. He will sell some of the computers. Some of the computers are not very good. Only a few people buy them at that time. Grewal says that it is OK. The computers show that if you work hard, you will be successful one day. Difficult words: collect (to put similar things together), childhood (the time when someone is a child), successful (to do something with a good result). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists in Europe are testing bio-based fertilizers made from algae grown on wastewater, showing they can cut mineral fertilizer use by 25% while keeping crop yields steady. In France, algae are cultivated on dairy effluents , where they feed on organic matter. The algae are then dried into powder and spread on fields, providing nitrogen naturally. Trials on wheat show that algae alone cannot match mineral fertilizers, but when combined, they achieve the same results while reducing mineral input. Compared to mineral fertilizers, algae powder releases nutrients more slowly, requiring farmers to plan and use more expertise . Still, its transportability and potential in regions with restrictions on sewage sludge make it promising. Projects such as WALNUT are testing these methods across Europe, including Spain’s advanced Ourense water plant. Here, researchers recover nitrogen and phosphorus from wastewater, transforming them into usable fertilizers like ammonium sulphate. These innovations could reduce pollution, cut energy use, and strengthen Europe’s independence from imports. Difficult words: effluent (waste liquid from factories or farms), expertise (special knowledge or skill in a subject), sewage sludge (thick, dirty water left after cleaning water from houses and factories). Researchers in Europe are making new fertilizers from algae that grow on wastewater. In France, farmers test algae powder made from dairy waste. The algae eat the organic matter, then become a powder rich in nitrogen . This powder, when mixed with mineral fertilizers, keeps the same crop yield but reduces mineral use by 25%. Algae powder is slower than normal fertilizer, so farmers need more planning and skill. But they can move it to other places and use it where sewage sludge is not allowed. In Spain, scientists at a water plant in Ourense recover nitrogen and phosphorus from wastewater and turn them into ammonium sulphate for farming. These new methods may cut pollution, save energy, and help Europe depend less on imports. Difficult words: fertilizer (food for plants), nitrogen (gas in the air which plants need to grow), yield (food or products which a farm or factory produces), sewage sludge (thick, dirty water left after cleaning water from houses and factories). A serious accident happened in Lisbon when the Glória funicular , a well-known tourist attraction, derailed and crashed into a building. Sixteen people lost their lives, and more than 20 others were injured. At least six remain in critical condition. The victims included British, Portuguese, South Koreans, Canadians, a Swiss, a Ukrainian, an American, and a French national. The cause of the disaster is still unclear. The capital’s public transport operator, Carris, explained that the funicular had passed both regular and comprehensive safety inspections, including a check only hours before the crash. Despite this, the vehicle lost control and slammed into the hillside building. Investigators are now examining possible failures, including a detached cable or problems with the braking system. Portuguese police confirmed that crimes are under consideration, particularly negligent homicide , if maintenance duties were not properly carried out. However, they emphasized that there is no current evidence of intentional wrongdoing. Difficult words: funicular (a small train that goes up and down a steep hill on tracks, usually for tourists), comprehensive (very complete, with many details), negligent homicide (when someone dies because another person or company didn’t take enough care or responsibility). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Still, the funicular ran down the hill and caused this disaster. Police think that a cable problem or broken brakes could be the reason. They also say there might be a crime if the company didn’t take good care of the system. Difficult words: funicular (a small train that goes up and down a steep hill on tracks), regular (happening often and at the same time), inspection (a careful check). Giorgio Armani, one of the world’s most renowned fashion designers, has passed away at the age of 91. Known as King Giorgio, he transformed menswear in the 1970s by softening the traditional jacket, creating a more relaxed and natural style. His idea that elegance means simplicity guided his career for five decades. Armani built a fashion empire that included haute couture , perfumes, home interiors, and hotels, making Italian fashion a global phenomenon . Born in 1934 in Piacenza, Armani moved to Milan after World War II. He first studied medicine but left the university and later entered the fashion industry by chance, working at the department store La Rinascente. His big break came with designer Nino Cerruti. In 1975, he launched his own label, later gaining fame in Hollywood with Richard Gere’s film American Gigolo. Despite his success, Armani kept control of his company, refusing to sell shares. His heirs include family members and close collaborators, and his brand is expected to continue. Difficult words: haute couture (very exclusive, handmade, luxury fashion), phenomenon (something amazing and important), heir (a person who receives property or business after someone dies). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

He was born in 1934 in Piacenza and later moved to Milan. He studied medicine but left and started to work in fashion. After helping designer Nino Cerruti, he opened his own label in 1975. His designs appeared in Hollywood films, and many stars wore his suits. Armani never sold his company and wanted it to stay independent . His family and close team will continue his work. Difficult words: symbol (a sign which represents something), label (a fashion brand or company), independent (free, not controlled by others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: fashion designer (a person who designs clothes), furniture (things like chairs, tables, or beds), private (not shared by others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Mexico has elected Hugo Aguilar as the first indigenous chief justice in over 150 years, following the country’s first judicial elections, where judges were chosen by popular vote. Aguilar, from the Mixtec community, has expertise in agrarian law and indigenous rights. His appointment represents hope for the one in five indigenous Mexicans who have historically been underrepresented in top positions. Many see this as a historic opportunity for inclusion in the Supreme Court. However, the process has sparked criticism. Critics argue that the ruling party, Morena, politicized the judiciary by supporting candidates aligned with its interests. Aguilar has also faced scrutiny for his previous role in managing complaints from indigenous communities regarding a controversial tourist train project, where some believe he defended the project over community rights. Over the next two years, Aguilar will have to demonstrate whether he truly represents marginalized groups or primarily the establishment. His role could significantly shape the future of justice and indigenous representation in Mexico. Difficult words: expertise (special knowledge or skill in a particular subject or area), appointment (officially giving someone a job or position), underrepresented (not having enough presence), politicized (made into a political issue). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hugo Aguilar becomes Mexico’s first indigenous chief justice in more than 150 years. He comes from the Mixtec community and knows agrarian law and indigenous rights. The political party Morena helped support him and other judges who agree with the party. Aguilar also had a past role in a project with a tourist train that some indigenous people didn’t like. Critics say he helped the project instead of the communities. In the next two years, he will need to show whether he will support indigenous people or mainly the government. His decisions may affect justice in Mexico. Difficult words: chief justice (the main judge), agrarian (related to farming), historic (very important). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Poland and pledged strong support to countries bordering Russia and Belarus. She announced plans for a modern European Union budget over the next seven years, which will significantly increase funding for migration and border management, military mobility , and defense investment. Countries directly bordering Russia and Belarus will receive additional European support, because Europe’s borders are a shared responsibility. Von der Leyen detailed that investment in migration and border protection will triple, funding for military mobility will increase tenfold, and defense investment overall will rise five times. This strategy aims to strengthen border security and military readiness across the EU, particularly for nations facing direct risks from neighboring regions. The commitment highlights the EU’s approach to collective responsibility, coordination, and long-term strategic planning to manage potential threats. By investing in both civil and military infrastructure, the European Union seeks to maintain stability and enhance cooperation among member states facing geopolitical pressures. Difficult words: pledge (to promise), mobility (the ability to move freely), readiness (being ready or prepared for something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Countries near Russia and Belarus will get extra funding because Europe’s borders are a shared responsibility . Von der Leyen explained that money for migration and border management will be three times bigger, for military movement ten times bigger, and for defense five times bigger. These actions will make borders safer and prepare countries for possible problems. The plan shows that the European Union wants countries to work together and be ready for challenges. Difficult words: defense (keeping safe from danger or attack), funding (money for a specific purpose), responsibility (a duty or something you must take care of). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Denmark’s national postal service, PostNord, will stop delivering letters at the end of the year, ending four centuries of letter deliveries. This decision comes as letter volumes have dropped by 90% since 2000. Around a third of the workforce, 1,500 employees, will lose their jobs, while 700 new positions will be created in the profitable parcel business. Online shopping and digital communication are key reasons for this change, as Danes increasingly rely on apps and digital mailboxes . The transition reflects a global trend: physical mail is declining in many countries, with a 30–70% drop in major markets. Private companies, such as Deo, will take over the remaining letter deliveries, but concerns exist for the quarter of a million people who still rely on physical post. PostNord’s shift highlights the challenges traditional postal services face in a rapidly digitizing society. Difficult words: profitable (making money or giving a financial benefit), digital mailbox (a virtual place on the internet where you receive letters or messages instead of papers), digitizing (changing information into digital form). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Denmark is very digital, and many letters go through online mailboxes . Private companies, like Deo, will deliver letters, but some people may have problems using digital mail. This trend is not only in Denmark; many countries see fewer letters every year. PostNord’s change shows how digital technology and online shopping can change old services and jobs, and it gives an example of what may happen in other countries in the future. Difficult words: delivery (bringing letters or parcels to someone), online mailbox (a place on the internet where you get letters or messages), trend (a general change). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 70 million people worldwide stutter , which is about one percent of the global population. Five percent of all children go through a period of stuttering, and most recover by late childhood. However, some have a long-term stutter, and scientists still don’t fully understand why. They studied the brains of people who stutter or who recovered from a stutter; they found they are different from the brains of people who don’t. This study means that a stutter has a neurological origin, and it comes from genetic differences. The condition often runs in families, and some of the genetic differences are related to sex. Men are more likely to stutter as children and more likely to continue to stutter into adulthood. The treatment of stutter differs and depends on whether the person is a young child very close to onset , a school-aged child, or an adult. Some techniques can help reduce the stutter; however, they don’t fix the neurological differences. Therapies help people understand that what they say is far more important than how they say it. However, society isn’t always accepting and supportive. Difficult words: stutter (to speak with difficulty, for example, to pause before saying a word or repeat it several times), neurological (related to the brain and the nervous system), onset (the beginning of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Reports say that 70 million people worldwide stutter. This is about one percent of the whole population. People who stutter have problems when they speak. Usually, they make a pause before they say a difficult word, or they repeat the same word several times. Scientists found that these people have different brains, so you cannot always stop a stutter. More people in one family often stutter, so the condition is genetic , too. Interestingly, men stutter three times more than women, but scientists don’t really know why. People can learn some techniques , which make their stutter less obvious , but these techniques don’t change the brain. They learn to understand that what we speak is more important rather than how we say. Difficult words: genetic (genes or information in the body that pass from one parents to children), techniques (the way to do something), obvious (something that people can see). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People learn some techniques to speak better. They must understand that they can’t change their brain. Also, they must understand that what you say is more important than how you say it. Difficult words: pause (the time between two actions), common (usual), technique (how people do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite the popularity of action titles like Fortnite or GTA, survival horror continues to attract loyal fans. At Gamescom in Germany, players explained that these games offer not only fear but also atmosphere, responsibility, and emotional stories. Developers agreed that horror must constantly evolve to keep audiences interested. Silent Hill F takes the series to 1960s Japan, adding cultural strangeness and focusing on psychological terror. Written by the Japanese author Ryukishi07, it emphasizes mystery and inner fear rather than fast action. This design avoids turning the game into a typical combat challenge, instead highlighting tension and emotional impact. Resident Evil Requiem marks the 30th anniversary of the franchise . It returns to Raccoon City, offering improved graphics, two camera modes, and a vulnerable main character named Grace. Developers stressed that their goal is to create horror-first experiences, not action-first ones, showing that survival horror still has a strong identity. Difficult words: evolve (to change slowly into something better), emphasize (to give importance to something), franchise (a series of games, movies, or books that belong to the same world or story). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Silent Hill F moves the game into 1960s Japan. It brings a new culture and focuses more on the mind than on action. The story comes from writer Ryukishi07, who is known for dark stories. Resident Evil Requiem celebrates 30 years of the series. It shows Raccoon City again, has better graphics , two ways to play (first-person and third-person), and a normal woman named Grace as the hero . The creators want horror to stay the main point. Difficult words: spirit (the main idea or feeling of something), graphics (the pictures, images, or visuals in a game or on screen), hero (the main good character in a story). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
